newsitem.title: UK: IPE calls for Nov gas oil delivery investigation.
newsitem.headline: IPE calls for Nov gas oil delivery investigation.

text.p: The directors of the International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) said in a statement that they have called for an investigation into the November gas oil delivery.
The call follows defaults arising out of the delivery of the November 1996 gas oil contract.
The directors said the London Clearing House (LCI) has referred to them a number of defaults attributable to the November gas oil delivery programme.

"Under the provisions of the IPE Rules, the Directors have determined a price at which the quantity of gas oil to which each default relates shall be invoiced back, without reference to the fault of either the seller or the buyer," the directors said in a statement.

Monte Carlo-based AIC and a Swiss unit of U.S.-based Cargill -- two big trading houses long known as rivals for supremacy in the trade in gas oil -- were involved in the bulk of a record high 865,100 tonne delivery due between November 16 and 30 on the Rotterdam barge market.

"Serious questions have been raised about the extent to which the seller and buyer involved in these defaults have complied with the regulations and the administrative procedures of the IPE," the directors said.

"The Directors, therefore, have instructed that an immediate investigation be conducted by the Exchange into the November gas oil delivery. Depending on the outcome of this investigation the IPE may commence disciplinary proceedings or take disciplinary action in respect of a member, or members of the Exchange."
